macro.syntax.command.title: Commands & parameters
macro.syntax.command.description: One registered command call per line. Supply parameters in declaration order; trailing optional parameters may be omitted. Macros cannot call other macros. Ordinary calls do not await asynchronous results.
macro.syntax.string.title: Strings and escaping
macro.syntax.string.description: Enclose strings in quotes. A backslash escapes quotes, backslashes and characters such as newlines. // inside a string does not start a comment.
macro.syntax.comment.title: // Comments
macro.syntax.comment.description: // may occupy a whole line or follow a command. Comments are not executed. Inline comments share the statement color; standalone comments use the body text color.
macro.syntax.comment.example:
// Standalone comment
WaitFor() // Wait for the next frame
macro.syntax.repeat.description: Repeat commands up to EndRepeat(). The count must be an integer literal from {Config_MIN_MACRO_REPEAT_COUNT} to {Config_MAX_MACRO_REPEAT_COUNT}. Nesting is not supported; multiple separate loops may appear in sequence. Without WaitFor, execution is continuous with no automatic frame yielding.
macro.syntax.endRepeat.description: End the current Repeat loop. No parameters are accepted; a matching Repeat is required. Shares its syntax color with Repeat.
macro.syntax.waitFrame.description: Wait until the next frame before executing the next line. Inside a loop, wait one frame each time this statement is reached.
macro.syntax.waitSeconds.title: WaitFor(seconds)
macro.syntax.waitSeconds.description: Wait for a finite, non-negative number of seconds, independently of timeScale. Accepts a seconds literal or a command call.
macro.syntax.waitCommand.title: WaitFor(command call)
macro.syntax.waitCommand.description: Call a command once and wait for completion. Supports Task, UniTask, their generic forms and IEnumerator. Synchronous methods complete when they return; UniTaskVoid cannot be awaited. Stopping a macro does not forcibly terminate business methods.
